title: "Functional areas"
---

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from pathlib import Path
from _helpers import fig, table, HERE
```

Each panel has two heatmaps. Left: the mean number of proteins carrying a domain per genome, per group, on a log2(x + 1) scale. Right: the log2 ratio of the group's mean copies per 10,000 genes to the all-genome mean (red = more than average, blue = fewer), which shows differences even for domains present in nearly every genome. The share of genomes carrying each domain is in `tables/<level>/T09_functional_panel.tsv` (`fraction_genomes`). Accessions were checked against the Pfam names stored in the BFD data.

## Curated domain panels

Kinases and signalling, transporters, cytochrome P450 and redox, transcription factors, scaffolds, chromatin and DNA metabolism, carbohydrate-active domains, peptidases, secondary metabolism, lipid metabolism, secreted and effector-like domains, and trehalose and carbon storage.

```{python}
for p in sorted((HERE / "figures" / "phylum").glob("F22_*.png")):
    fig(p.stem, p.stem.split("_panel_", 1)[-1].replace("_", " ").capitalize(), "80%")
```

```{python}
table("T09_functional_panel", link_pfam="pfam_acc", max_rows=60, levels=["phylum"])
```

The full panel tables are `tables/<level>/T09_functional_panel.tsv`.

## Intrinsic disorder

```{python}
fig("F23_idp_fraction", "Mean fraction of each protein predicted as intrinsically disordered, per genome.")
fig("F23b_idp_gt03", "Share of proteins with an intrinsic-disorder fraction above 0.3.")
```

Disorder scores exist for roughly 60% of proteins; a protein with no row is read as "no disordered region", which fits the pattern with protein length but has not been confirmed against the predictor's rules. Residue counts are not used here for that reason.
